question: Why has no saffron crocus ever been grown from its own seed?
answer: Because it is a sterile triploid, with three sets of chromosomes, and sets no viable seed. Every plant is a clone, multiplied from underground corms. A 2019 genetic study traced the crop to wild Crocus cartwrightianus near Athens: fields from Kashmir to La Mancha grow copies of one ancient plant.
move: Where every plant is a copy, one disease can meet no resistance.
source: Nemati et al., Mol. Phylogenet. Evol., 2019
reference: Nemati et al., Saffron (Crocus sativus) is an autotriploid that evolved in Attica (Greece) from wild Crocus cartwrightianus, Molecular Phylogenetics and Evolution, 2019
